title: tb-scaffold.json contract (post-materialize)
description: Structural contract for asic/<module>/Verification/simulation-plan/tb-scaffold.json, validated by the check-scaffold gate AFTER the materialize-scaffold verb has run. The sequence roster and the power scenarios live in their own files (sequences.json / power-scenarios.json); what remains here is what simulation alone reads. Every field below says whether it is yours to author or script-injected, and carries the authoring judgment no validator can express. Strongly validates LLM-authored fields; tolerates (does not deep-validate) the interface/transaction objects materialize-scaffold injects into agents[] (their content is owned by materialize-scaffold + sim/_guards._agent_io). Referential integrity (observer/inports/seqs resolving to declared agents, and sequences.json/power-scenarios.json resolving against each other) is NOT expressible here; the check-scaffold gate's semantic layer enforces it.

mode.description: `active` for a driver/master group you drive, `passive` for a monitor/slave group you only observe. Take it from the group's top-io.json `direction` values.

interface_groups.description: top-io.json `interface_group` names. Ports sharing a group become one virtual interface and this one agent.

interface.description: Script-injected by `simplan materialize-scaffold` (never hand-authored): every signal of every declared group, name and width verbatim from top-io.json.

transaction.description: Script-injected by `simplan materialize-scaffold` (never hand-authored): the same signals minus clk/rst, which must never be rand txn fields.

feature.description: The features.json id this test exercises. Required, and it must resolve: it is the key materialize-scaffold reads feature_name through (an id that resolves to nothing fails it loud), and the only thing that makes a result traceable.

test_id.description: Stable per-test identifier; the regression log keys results by it.

suites.description: Which suites run this test — `["smoke", "regress"]` or `["regress"]`. YOUR judgment as the plan author, not a script's: `make smoke` is the fast pre-check, `make regress` runs everything. A smoke test is one whose failure means the design is broken badly enough that running the rest is pointless — the datapath itself, or the register path every other test loads its stimulus through. Pick them by that, not by position in the list; most modules need two or three.

feature_name.description: Script-injected by `simplan materialize-scaffold` (never hand-authored): the matching features.json entry's `name`, verbatim. It is what the Feature column of case-results-summary.md prints, so a human reads this rather than a bare id.

inports.description: The agents[].name values whose monitor streams feed the RM — one analysis_imp port each. YOUR judgment: which agents feed the reference model. Name the AGENT, not its transaction type: simulation's renderer builds the type as <module>_<agent>_txn where it needs one, so a name written here in txn form would have to be un-wrapped and re-wrapped to reach the same string. The gate only checks the names resolve.

observer.description: The ONE agents[].name whose monitor stream the scoreboard compares against the RM. Omitted only when a single agent is declared; with more than one, omitting it is ambiguous and the gate rejects it.

primary_clock.description: Script-injected by `simplan materialize-scaffold` (never hand-authored): the clocks.json entry with relationship=="primary".

reset.description: Script-injected by `simplan materialize-scaffold` (never hand-authored): the top-io.json entry with role=="reset".

intent.description: What this testpoint drives and why — the stimulus/intent the env and conformance-fix children read as the intent source. Write the situation being created, not the check: `inlined_check_hints` already says how each covered check is verified.

bins.description: The coverage bins this testpoint is meant to hit, as your own tags. Simulation's verify child reads them alongside `intent` when it judges whether an uncovered branch or FSM transition falls inside any testpoint's remit, so write what the testpoint covers rather than urg's identifiers; an item it cannot place is routed back here as a missing testpoint.

covers.description: The `check-hints/<child>.json` check_ids this testpoint verifies — YOUR clustering (one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-one). The clustering is also what makes a testpoint traceable: present with an explicit empty array on a scenario testpoint you invented, since omitted and `[]` are not the same claim, and an empty one verifies no authored check and so traces to no feature. Say that deliberately; it is not a default.

inlined_check_hints.description: Script-injected by `simplan materialize-scaffold` (never hand-authored): the precise check semantics from the authored `check-hints/<child>.json`, materialized into this testpoint via its `covers[]`. `implementation_detail` is verbatim-if-present-else-summary. The feature a testpoint traces to is NOT copied in: the plan-review reviewer resolves it from covers[] + the authored check hints, both of which it already reads.

skipped_checks.description: Every check_hints[] check_id no testpoint covers, each with why. The coverage-matrix gate accepts a check_id only as covered or skipped, so this is where a check that has no runtime testpoint is accounted for.

reason.description: Why no testpoint verifies it, e.g. "static lint gate, no runtime testpoint".
